title: Rigidity of morphisms between constant derived complexes on the affine line
statement:
Fix the algebraically closed field $k$ and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $p:T=\mathbf A^1_k\to s$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use bounded constructible complexes of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and exact derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. For $P,Q\in D^b_c(s_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and any morphism $v:p^*P\to p^*Q$ in $D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the restrictions at any $a,b\in k$ are equal:
$$i_a^*v=i_b^*v:P\longrightarrow Q,$$
where $i_c:s\to T$ is the section with coordinate $c$, and $i_c^*p^*$ is identified with the identity through $p i_c=1_s$. No finite Tor amplitude hypothesis is imposed on $P$ or $Q$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.4, specialized to X=affine line and Y=Spec k; bounded finite-module version without a perfectness assumption.

proof.text: Work first in the ambient derived categories of small etale A-module sheaves. The point s has the trivial etale topos: by [lem-kun-0ezp] each etale s-scheme U is a disjoint union of copies of s. The sheaf axiom for that covering gives F(U)=product_{u in U} F(s), naturally in U. Thus evaluation at s and the constant-module sheaf functor are inverse equivalences, also on A-module sheaves since the action is evaluated componentwise. They are exact inverse equivalences and therefore remain inverse when applied termwise to complexes and localized at quasi-isomorphisms. We henceforth identify D(s_et,A) with D(A) and Rp_* with RΓ(T,-) under this identification. In particular RΓ(s,Q)=Q; this uses no projectivity or finite Tor dimension of Q.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.4, specialization Y=Spec k; point-topos identification expanded using Stacks Tag 0EZP.

proof.text: First establish that the canonical etale unit η^e_A:A_s→Rp_{et,*}A_T of the derived adjunction p^*⊣Rp_* of [def-kun-kunneth-map] is invertible. The base field and finite ring in [def-pur-conventions] agree with the present k,A. Apply [lem-pur-affine-line-ordinary-invariance] with X=s and r=0; on the small etale site A(0)_X=A_X by definition [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], so the adjunction unit A_s→Rp_*A_T is an isomorphism. This unit is η^e_A: by the Hom bijection of [def-kun-kunneth-map], for a degree-zero sheaf F on s and a K-injective resolution p^{-1}F→I, the derived unit is F→p_*p^{-1}F→p_*I, the sheaf unit followed by the edge map, with p^{-1}A_s identified with A_T by [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. No boundedness hypothesis is involved, since A_s is a single sheaf in degree zero.

source.place: Statement (affine-line acyclicity of the constant coefficient), in the small etale form recorded by lem-pur-affine-line-ordinary-invariance for X=Spec k, r=0.

proof.text:
For arbitrary Q as in the statement apply [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring] to X=T, Y=s, K=A_T and L=Q. Both schemes are separated finite-type over k, and its finite ring is exactly A; its categories are unbounded and it imposes no finite Tor hypothesis. Use the constant-pullback identification [lem-kun-pullback-constant] and the canonical tensor-unit constraints [lem-kun-tensor-unit] to obtain the canonical isomorphism κ_Q:Rp_*A_T⊗_A^L Q→Rp_*p^*Q. Consider
Q≅A⊗_A^L Q --(η^e_A⊗1)--> Rp_*A_T⊗_A^L Q --κ_Q--> Rp_*p^*Q.
This composite is exactly η^e_Q, not merely some isomorphism between the two objects. In fact [def-kun-kunneth-map] defines κ as the adjunct of the tensor product of the pulled-back counits. The adjunct of the displayed composite is therefore the tensor product of ε^e_{A_T} p^*(η^e_A)=id_{A_T} (the triangle identity) and the identity on p^*Q (the Y=s structure map is the identity). After the same unit constraints this is id_{p^*Q}, whose adjunct is η^e_Q. Step 2 and Kunneth now show that η^e_Q is invertible, even when Q is nonperfect.

source.place: Statement, with X=affine line, Y=Spec k, K=A_T, L=Q; the canonical-map definition is expanded via its two counits.

proof.text: Use the derived module adjunction p^*⊣Rp_* specified in [def-kun-kunneth-map]. Given v:p^*P→p^*Q, its adjunct is Rp_*(v) η^e_P. Put w=(η^e_Q)^{-1} Rp_*(v) η^e_P:P→Q. Naturality of η gives that the adjunct of p^*w is η^e_Q w=Rp_*(v) η^e_P. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection yields v=p^*w. The objects P,Q lie in the bounded constructible full subcategory, so w is a morphism there too. This is a direct calculation with the adjunction, not an internal-Hom tensor formula requiring a dualizable P.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.4, affine-line/point case: replace the internal-Hom shortcut by the adjunction Hom bijection.

proof.text: For any c∈k, pi_c=id_s. The canonical sheaf composition maps and identity map of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition](2),(3) give i_c^*p^*≅id. Their module lifts are the natural A-linear maps of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear](2); applying them termwise descends to derived inverse image as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. Naturality with respect to w gives i_c^*(p^*w)=w under exactly these canonical identifications. Step 4 therefore gives i_a^*v=w=i_b^*v. The equality holds in the full bounded constructible subcategory used in the statement. No step imposed a Tor-amplitude condition on P or Q.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.4, equality of restrictions at points; canonical composition identifications made explicit.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 3.1.4 specialized to X=A1, Y=Spec k; expanded using affine-line acyclicity, finite-ring unbounded Kunneth, and adjunction to avoid a perfectness assumption.
